messages:
maria_p: FYI — Customer (AcmeDocs) migrating from OpenAI -> Redwood. Their integration started failing on tool calls. They say the model returns lowercase enum values and our strict schema validation rejects them. Attached repro below.

alex.k: can you paste the request/response and the server error?

maria_p: sure — repro curl and payload: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{\n    "model":"gpt-compat-1",\n    "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Create a doc"}],\n    "functions":[{\n      "name":"doc_action",\n      "parameters":{\n        "type":"object",\n        "properties":{\n          "action":{"type":"string","enum":["CREATE","UPDATE","DELETE"]},\n          "resource_id":{"type":"string"}\n        },\n        "required":["action","resource_id"]\n      }\n    }]\n  }'
```

maria_p: model returned a function call: 
```
{"name":"doc_action","arguments":"{\"action\":\"create\",\"resource_id\":\"123\"}"}
```

maria_p: our runtime log shows validation error when attempting to map the function args to the declared schema: 
```
[error] validation failed: enum value 'create' not in allowed set ['CREATE','UPDATE','DELETE']
400 Bad Request - invalid_function_call_args
```

jordan_r: oh interesting — OpenAI historically accepted case-insensitive enum strings in some SDKs, customers assumed that. We treat enums strictly.

alex.k: customer impact?

maria_p: their app retries on 400 which inflated their bill and caused latency spikes. They flagged as Sev2.

eng-ml: tagging in. Two paths: (1) add a compat normalizer that uppercases enum strings for OpenAI-compatible model responses, or (2) add a lenient enum parsing option per-customer. Both require careful gating to avoid semantics issues.

alex.k: is there already an experiment/flag for lenient parsing?

jordan_r: we have an internal config `openai_compat_mode` that maps a few things (null vs missing, stringified args) but enum aliasing was avoided due to risk. We did prototype `enum_aliases` mapping in dev branch.

support-bot: Ticket #S-44321 created for AcmeDocs. Priority: P2 (customer billing spike).

alex.k: can you share a minimal fix we can ship quickly? Customer needs a workaround today.

maria_p: suggested interim workaround: update their function schema to accept lowercase variants too (add enum entries `create`,`update`,`delete`) OR add a preprocessor in their integration to uppercase `action` before calling the function. I sent both options.

eng-ml: engineering plan: short term - implement a small middleware in the compat layer that will, when `openai_compat_mode` is enabled, normalize enum strings by doing a case-insensitive match against enum values and coerce to canonical case. Will gate behind customer opt-in. Long term - consider a compatibility flag in model routing that applies a safer set of normalizations.

alex.k: can eng-runtime add a logging metric to count how many function calls are rejected for enum mismatches so we can quantify impact?

ops-bot: created metric `compat.enum_mismatch.count` (temp dashboard link: https://dash.internal/enum-mismatch).

jordan_r: note — we should also update docs/FAQ about OpenAI compatibility quirks (enum casing, stringified args, missing fields).

maria_p: customer accepted the temporary workaround (they'll patch enums on their side) and would like opt-in when available. I'll keep ticket open and mark to follow up when eng deploys the compat flag.

alex.k: assigned to eng-ml and eng-runtime for implementation and to triage risk. @eng-ml @jordan_r please sync on design doc. :eyes:

eng-ml: will draft a short RFC and post in #eng-ml, cc @alex.k.

maria_p: thanks all — keeping this thread updated with any customer feedback.

support-bot: Ticket #S-44321 updated: status -> escalated; assignees -> eng-ml, eng-runtime.
